source:
Create a 3D Stage-Based Brainrot Parkour Game with Spawning Timers, 3 Difficulty Zones, and a Pet Collection System.
​CRITICAL GAME RULES & MECHANICS:
​1. PET SPAWNING & DESPAWN TIMERS (STRICT MECHANIC):
​All pets/rewards spawned in the world must have a 30-second despawn timer after appearing. If no player collects them within 30 seconds, they disappear until the next respawn cycle.
​Zone 1 & Zone 2 Pets: Respawn regularly every 1 to 2 minutes with a 30-second collection window.
​SPECIAL OG PET (Strawberry Elephant): Spawns EXCLUSIVELY once every 5 minutes in Zone 3 (Impossible Stage). It stays active for exactly 30 seconds before despawning. Add a visible 3D countdown timer above its spawn pad so players know when it will appear!
​2. ZONE 1: NORMAL STAGE (Easy Parkour Course)
​Build a simple floating platform parkour.
​End Rewards Area (Physical 3D Machine / Spawner):
​Common Pets: Cactus Elephant (green blocky elephant made of cactus blocks with brown ears) & Brr Brr Patapim / Noob (yellow blocky character with blue torso, green legs, and flat orange hat).
​Rare Pets: Gangster Footera (blocky character with black sunglasses, gold chain, and blue jacket) & Wise Gnome (blocky green creature with a long white beard and yellow eyes).
​3. ZONE 2: HARD STAGE (Medium/Hard Parkour Course)
​Build a challenging parkour course with moving platforms and lava hazard blocks.
​End Rewards Area (Physical 3D Machine / Spawner):
​Tralalero Tralala: A blocky blue shark on legs wearing blue sneakers.
​Tung Tung Sahur: A cylindrical wooden totem character holding a baseball bat.
​4. ZONE 3: IMPOSSIBLE STAGE (Extreme Parkour Course)
​Build an extreme obstacle course with very long jumps and tiny platforms.
​End Rewards Area (Secret OG Spawner Pad):
​Strawberry Elephant (100% OG Rarity): A bright red blocky elephant covered in sparkles with green leaves on its head.
​Reminding rule: Spawns ONLY every 5 minutes for 30 seconds!
​5. GENERAL SYSTEM:
​Players gain Coins and Speed by completing stages.
​Collected 3D Pets follow the player and grant Speed and Coin multipliers.
​NO 2D UI menus for shops/pets; everything must be physical 3D stations built into the world map!

answers.ask: Are the three zones one continuous map you walk between, or separate places you teleport to?
answers.answer: Make the three zones part of one continuous floating parkour map that players walk between, with Zone 1 leading into Zone 2 and then Zone 3.

answers.ask: Does the game end after zone 3, or loop for pet collection?
answers.answer: It loops for pet collection; completing Zone 3 does not end the game, and players can replay stages while waiting for spawn cycles.
Keep each course short and replayable: about 1–2 minutes for Zone 1, 2–3 minutes for Zone 2, and 3–4 minutes for Zone 3.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D stage-based parkour map as one continuous floating course, with Zone 1 leading directly into Zone 2 and then Zone 3. Zone 1 is a simple floating-platform course lasting about 1–2 minutes, ending at a physical reward-spawner machine displaying common and rare blocky pet figures: a green cactus-block elephant with brown ears, a yellow noob-like figure with blue torso, green legs and flat orange hat, a sunglasses-and-gold-chain character in a blue jacket, and a green gnome-like creature with a long white beard and yellow eyes. Zone 2 is a 2–3 minute harder course with moving platforms and lava hazard blocks, ending at another physical spawner with a blue shark on legs in blue sneakers and a cylindrical wooden totem holding a baseball bat. Zone 3 is a 3–4 minute extreme course of very long jumps and tiny platforms, ending at a secret OG spawner pad for a sparkling bright-red blocky elephant with green leaves on its head; place a visible 3D countdown timer above this pad. Include physical 3D pet and reward stations throughout the map, with room for replay loops back toward earlier stages.

## Genre

The dominant genre is Obby & Platformer because difficulty comes from completing real parkour geometry. Simulation is secondary for the timed pet-collection and repeatable reward loop.

## Shape and preset

Use `course-flat`, one continuous floating point-to-point course divided into three sequential difficulty zones. The Classic Obby preset applies without checkpoints, supplemented by reward stations, lava, and replay circulation.

## Config requirements

Draw `path-track` through Zones 1, 2, and 3. Use `obstacle-jump` throughout, `obstacle-moving` in Zone 2, and `hazard-kill` for its lava blocks. Add `path-circulation` as a safe replay route from the Zone 3 end toward earlier stages. Draw three physical reward stations: Zone 1 displays four specified figures, Zone 2 displays two, and Zone 3 displays one sparkling red elephant on a secret pad beneath a visible 3D countdown timer.

## Layout requirements

Place four pet spawn sockets at the Zone 1 machine and two at Zone 2, each with a 30-second collection window and 1–2-minute respawn cycle. Place one exclusive Zone 3 pet socket, spawning every 5 minutes for exactly 30 seconds, directly under its countdown. Site each machine on a safe end platform clear of hazards. Place a replay return path from Zone 3 to the Zone 1 approach. Timing and follower bonuses are mechanics, but their physical pads and clearance are layout requirements.

## Layout components

Build three linked floating zones: a 1–2-minute simple platform run, a 2–3-minute moving-platform and lava run, and a 3–4-minute extreme run of tiny platforms and very long authored jumps. Each ends on a broad reward deck holding its machine and named pet displays. The final deck includes the secret red-elephant pad and overhead timer. Open fall space surrounds the route; no baseplate is present. A distinct safe loop-back walkway skirts the course to earlier zones. Compose the map diagonally so the escalating zones and all three reward decks read in sequence.

## Render order

Use `topdown`: plan the authoritative route first because all three courses and the replay loop must remain connected and completable, then dress it isometrically.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost

Scale is large, driven by three courses totaling about 6–9 minutes. The theme is colorful floating brainrot parkour with blocky collectible characters. Use `P6` for valid obstacle construction; the explicitly extreme long jumps require authored validation rather than ordinary baseline spacing.
